about.lead: This is 2FAS Share. It lets you share passwords and messages through an encrypted link, with no account or installation. Closing this window does not use up the link.
about.step1: The sender enters the content, and it is encrypted in their browser.
about.step2: The decryption key stays in the link itself, after the # sign. The browser never sends this part of the link to the server.
about.step3: Only encrypted content reaches our server, and we don't have the key to read it.
about.step4: You open the link, and the key decrypts the content on your device. The link expires after the time the sender chose, or after the first open if they set it that way.
about.title: How it works
about.warningBody: Anyone with the full link can open the message, so check an unexpected link with the sender through another channel.
about.warningTitle: The link works like a key.

encryption.lead: The key used to encrypt it stays in the link itself, in the part after the # sign. That is the part browsers never send to the server.
encryption.leadNote: Without the full link, no one can read it, not even us.
encryption.note: Keep in mind that anyone who gets the full link can open the message, so send it only to people you trust.
encryption.step1Desc: You enter the content. It is encrypted right away in your browser.
encryption.step2Desc: The decryption key stays in the link itself, after the # sign.
encryption.step3Desc: It only gets encrypted data. It never sees the key.
encryption.step4Desc: The key from the link decrypts the content in their browser.
encryption.stepsNote: Content is encrypted in your browser, and the key stays in the link itself, never on our server.
encryption.title: Encrypted before it leaves your device

faq.a1:
Content is encrypted in your browser before it leaves your device. The key stays in the link itself (after the # sign), and browsers don't send that part to our server. Your content reaches us only in encrypted form, and we don't have the key to read it.

Opening it takes the full link, and you can add a password for extra protection.
faq.a2: No. There is no sign-up and nothing to install. Enter the content, set the rules and create the link.
faq.a3: Yes. 2FAS Share is free to use, and you don't need an account. The code is open source, so anyone can check how it works.
faq.a4: You decide who gets the link. Opening it takes the full link, and the password if you set one. With one-time access on, the link stops working after the first open.
faq.a5: The link stops working and the encrypted content is removed from our server. Anyone who opens the link later will only see that it no longer works.
faq.a6: An email or a text message can stay in inboxes, backups and chat histories for years. A 2FAS Share link stops working after the first open or after the time you choose, and the content is end-to-end encrypted.
faq.a7: The link has already been opened or its time has run out. That's how 2FAS Share keeps your content protected. Just create a new link and send it again.
faq.q5: What happens after the link expires?
faq.q6: How is this different from email or a text message?
faq.q7: What if the recipient gets the error “This link no longer works”?
faq.title:
Quick answers on
2FAS Share
